result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right and that the real problem is one detailed master logo reused at sizes it wasn't drawn for. B covers more of the causes: it names thin strokes, gaps closing as the fabric puckers, small text, low-contrast colors and gradients, and gives concrete minimum sizes for stitching. A is tighter, fits a small firm better with its three-file scope, and includes a one-color test at 16px, but it never mentions color contrast or gradients and has an awkward phrase ('small-print-free'). | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the designer is partly right, put the blame on reusing one detailed master logo everywhere, and recommend a simplified icon plus an embroidery version. A explains the causes more fully, covering low contrast, gradients and gaps closing up, while B has a confusing line ('small-print-free') and a looser thread-width figure. B wins narrowly: its 'small project, three files' scope fits a small firm, and its test (checking the icon at 16/32px in one flat color on light and dark, plus a sample stitch-out viewed at arm's length) matches the rubric's quick-test item more closely.
